## Maintenance procedure

Every live schema/deployment/traffic change needs separate explicit approval for
its exact target, source/SQL hashes and effects. Merge, CI and an earlier closed
window are not fresh execution approval. Keep users running during preparation.

1. **Prepare:** verify merged source and passing CI, current schema dependencies,
   live deployment/env/LINE/protection bindings, fresh recovery and local rehearsal.
   Prepare an exact forward/inverse packet; use original migrations as history,
   not instructions to rerun them against the final production schema.
2. **Confirm the window:** name the supervising owner and reopening/abort deadline.
   Confirm browser/LINE users, direct Supabase editors, jobs and scripts are paused,
   with all pending saves/uploads finished or accounted for without uncertain
   provider outcomes. Pause external writers too; do not assume Vercel covers them.
3. **Fence and drain:** publish only the reviewed temporary rule denying methods
   other than GET/HEAD/OPTIONS. Verify browser mutations/LINE are denied, reads are
   available and active/prepared business transactions have drained. Preserve all
   original rules. LINE retries/WAF denial are not a durable event inbox; this
   procedure relies on the confirmed sender pause. Other event-hold arrangements
   need their own verified loss-safe procedure and approval.
4. **Reconcile:** match the complete frozen checkpoint, not only its revision.
   Capture the same four canonical GET baselines: orders, movements, shipments,
   employees. Keep response bodies private and transient; retain hashes, order,
   type and revision evidence. Stop or refresh recovery on drift.
5. **Apply:** execute only the reviewed operator artifact and hash-bound settings.
   Bind isolation/purpose/revision/source/recovery before and after writer/table
   locks; use the artifact's bounded timeouts. Unknown dependencies, role/ACL drift,
   partial schema or insufficient time are abort conditions. Inspect uncertain
   outcomes before retrying. Never silently repair records to pass a gate.
6. **Verify:** require all 51 table values and metadata unchanged except the
   explicitly approved schema delta, preserving owners/ACLs/RLS, journals, IDs,
   revisions and timestamps. Compare the four HTTP responses exactly. Do not
   replace signed-LINE/provider evidence with an unapproved real transaction.
7. **Reopen:** remove only this window's rule. Verify the original firewall,
   deployment/env, LINE cutoff/signature rejection and idempotency guards, plus read
   availability. Scan the actual live deployment's runtime error counts and save
   private receipts. Reopen users/jobs only after the checks pass.

published. Compare them against that exact active configuration; all protection
settings and original rules must remain unchanged. Do not disable a protection to
make a health check pass or create a broad deployment bypass.

## Rollback and refusal conditions

- Before commit, a failed guarded transaction must roll back atomically. Check
  actual schema state and transaction outcome rather than blindly resubmitting.
- After commit and before reopening, keep the fence active. Use only the reviewed,
  locally rehearsed schema-only inverse if its exact forward-state and revision
  gates still hold. Verify records and original metadata before reopening.
- After reopening, newer acknowledged writes must never be overwritten by an old
  dump or a switch back to stale Google Sheets. Stop, inspect journals/provider
  uncertainty and prepare an approved rollback/reconciliation against current data.
- Application rollback needs an exact compatible schema/deployment/config binding.
  Never assume an older build supports removed columns or new writes merely
  because its reads once passed. Current PR80 code supports the PR81 schema change;
  that specific compatibility is not a general permission to roll back releases.
- Keep protected staging, retained imports and unrelated resources untouched. No
  paid resource, account creation, provider action or fresh Sheets synchronization
  is authorized by this document.

# Project roadmap

## Completed database milestone

The Supabase production cutover and storage cleanup are complete through
[PR86](https://github.com/volkswg/stock-management/pull/86): stable IDs, native
timestamps, operational sidecar retirement, typed mappings and shared validation.
Browser writes and LINE are open. Old business Sheets remain read-only. Current
storage contracts and release gates live in the [runbook](../database-migration.md);
dated proof is in [progress](progress.md#latest-production-release).

Do not restart the migration, rerun import/retirement SQL or treat completed
cutover plans as pending work. Retained import tables, journals, credentials,
snapshots and recovery evidence remain protected. A later live change still needs
its own exact scope, fresh recovery/freshness review and execution approval.

## Current scoped work: order-bill identity

PR89 completed private account migration; business/account reads use PostgreSQL
and Drive uploads retain their provider ownership. PR90's first identity maintenance
was rolled back after its HTTP edit-revision UNION mixed text and bigint IDs.
Production is open on `f7f50b2`, with `order_bills.id` still text and all data preserved.

The focused correction casts revision identities to text and verifies actual HTTP
family/record tokens across the type transition. Release that corrected compatible
app first, then obtain fresh recovery/freshness verification and a new supervised
pause for the separately approved bigint conversion. Other table IDs stay unchanged.
[The runbook](../database-migration.md#order-bill-bigint-identity-prepared-not-activated)
contains sequence permissions, direct-editor requirements and rollback gates.

## Next major milestone: user authentication

The [authentication roadmap](../architecture/user-authentication-roadmap.md)
covers user login, secure sessions, roles, shop-level authorization, administration
and API access control. It remains planning only until separately approved.
Preserve current LINE signatures/cutoff, API restrictions, verified TLS and database
permissions. The owner's `legacy-as-is` release policy does not mean access gaps
are repaired or new exposure is authorized. [Issue38](https://github.com/volkswg/stock-management/issues/38)
retains the historical security tracking context.

## Deferred work and decisions

- Backup automation/failure-alert activation remains deferred. Verified one-off
  recovery checkpoints remain required for approved destructive maintenance.
- The cross-table Order/Movement revision-conflict fix was released in PR83.
  It uses record-scoped tokens and preserves same-record conflicts. See [evidence and release requirements](progress.md#concurrent-browser-edits-2026-11-18).
  Broader conflict-merging UI and other feature scopes remain deferred.
- Further removal of typed mapping functions needs an explicit adapter/consumer
  migration. Their current count alone is not a removal approval.
- Broader provider replacement, cross-provider transactions/queues, tenant/billing
  features and Workspace redesign need separate product decisions.
- Retained semantic service/script interfaces remain; business Sheets and positional
  adapter retirement are part of the currently approved native-storage conversion.

## Gates for future changes

Follow the [architecture rules](../architecture/rules.md) and [verification guide](verification.md).
Preserve financial/stock calculations, dates, IDs, routes/DTOs, LINE transitions,
retry/idempotency and provider ordering. Keep changes focused, use one reviewable
PR when practical, and distinguish implementation/merge from live execution.
Record new evidence once in [progress](progress.md). Historical phase descriptions
and prior local/CI results are indexed there rather than repeated as current plans.

"""Reconstruct the pinned pre-native source for immutable historical witnesses.

Never overlay the current checkout. Native acceptance loads real current source
separately on fresh final-schema databases.
"""
import hashlib,json,os,sys,subprocess
from pathlib import Path
ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
def digest(data):return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
def copy_history(target):
    target=Path(target)
    if target.exists() and any(target.iterdir()):raise ValueError('Historical destination must be empty')
    fixture=json.loads((ROOT/'tests/fixtures/native-postgres-before.json').read_text())
    followup=json.loads((ROOT/'tests/fixtures/native-null-json-before.json').read_text())
    accounts=json.loads((ROOT/'tests/fixtures/postgres-accounts-before.json').read_text())
    bills=json.loads((ROOT/'tests/fixtures/bill-identity-before.json').read_text())
    revision=json.loads((ROOT/'tests/fixtures/bill-revision-before.json').read_text())
    for name,expected in fixture['files'].items():
        edit=fixture['edits'].get(name)
        source=ROOT/name
        current=source.read_bytes() if source.exists() else None
        revision_edit=revision['edits'].get(name)
        if revision_edit:
            assert (digest(current) if current is not None else None)==revision_edit['afterSha256'],name
            current=revision_edit['before'].encode()
            assert digest(current)==revision_edit['beforeSha256'],name
        bill_edit=bills['edits'].get(name)
        if bill_edit:
            assert (digest(current) if current is not None else None)==bill_edit['afterSha256'],name
            current=bill_edit['before'].encode()
            assert digest(current)==bill_edit['beforeSha256'],name
        account_edit=accounts['edits'].get(name)
        if account_edit:
            assert (digest(current) if current is not None else None)==account_edit['afterSha256'],name
            current=account_edit['before'].encode()
            assert digest(current)==account_edit['beforeSha256'],name
        delta=followup['edits'].get(name)
        if delta:
            assert current is not None and digest(current)==delta['afterSha256'],name
            current=delta['before'].encode()
            assert digest(current)==delta['beforeSha256'],name
        if edit:
            if edit['afterSha256'] is None:assert current is None,name
            else:assert current is not None and digest(current)==edit['afterSha256'],name
            data=edit['before'].encode()
        else:data=current
        assert digest(data)==expected,name
        dest=target/name;dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);dest.write_bytes(data)
    os.symlink((ROOT/'node_modules').resolve(),target/'node_modules',target_is_directory=True)
    assert not list(target.glob('.env.*')) or {p.name for p in target.glob('.env.*')}=={'.env.example'}
    assert not (target/'.vercel').exists()
    # Some immutable acceptance tools attest HEAD/use git ls-files. Give this
    # owned fixture a credential-free synthetic Git identity, never the user's.
    env={'PATH':os.environ['PATH'],'GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM':'1','GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL':os.devnull,
         'GIT_AUTHOR_NAME':'Pinned Pre-native Fixture','GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL':'fixture@example.invalid',
         'GIT_COMMITTER_NAME':'Pinned Pre-native Fixture','GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL':'fixture@example.invalid'}
    def git(*args):subprocess.run(['git','-C',str(target),'-c','core.hooksPath=/dev/null',*args],env=env,check=True,stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    git('init','--quiet','--template=')
    names=list(fixture['files'])
    for i in range(0,len(names),50):git('add','--force','--',*names[i:i+50])
    git('commit','--quiet','--no-gpg-sign','-m','Synthetic source snapshot: pinned pre-native contracts')
    return target
if __name__=='__main__':copy_history(sys.argv[1])
